lesson.subject: data-ai
lesson.title: Fair and Responsible AI
lesson.summary: Find out how bias gets into AI, test for fairness, see why people stay responsible, and write a class pledge for fair and careful AI.
learning_objectives: Explain how unbalanced data and stereotypes can make AI biased
Plan a fair test that compares results for different groups
Explain that people stay responsible and write a class AI pledge

standards.text: Societal impact: AI can impact the world in positive and negative ways, and fairness matters
Use technology safely, respectfully and responsibly; recognise acceptable and unacceptable behaviour

success_criteria: I can say what bias and a stereotype are
I can plan a fair test and compare groups
I know people are responsible, and I can write a fair AI pledge
lesson.real_life: Noticing when a voice helper or a picture app works better for some people than others, and telling a trusted adult.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do we make AI fair?
blocks.say: Today we ask: can AI be unfair? And what can people do about it?

blocks.alt: An old black iron weighing scale holding a bowl of grain on a rustic wooden counter in a dim room
blocks.caption: A scale should weigh everything in the same fair way. AI should treat people fairly too.
blocks.credit: Photo by Kellen Riggin on Unsplash
blocks.say: A fair scale weighs everything the same way. Zara's class wants AI that treats everyone fairly too.

blocks.markdown: **Bias** is an unfair leaning in how an AI works.
blocks.say: AI learns from data. If the data leaves some people out, the AI may work badly for them. That unfairness is called bias.

scenes.caption: One town.
scenes.say: A class trains a voice reader with recordings from only one town.

scenes.caption: Gaps.
scenes.say: It understands that town's voices very well. It struggles with voices from other places.

scenes.caption: The cause.
scenes.say: The program did not choose to be unfair. Its training data had gaps.

question.prompt: A voice reader was trained with recordings from only one town. What may happen?
question.hint: Think about what it learned from.
question.explanation: Missing voices in the training data can cause bias.

options.text: It will work perfectly for everyone
It may work worse for other voices

blocks.markdown: A **stereotype** is a fixed idea about a group of people.
blocks.say: A stereotype is a fixed idea about a group. A story helper may copy stereotypes from the text it learned.
For example, it might always make the pilot a boy. That is unfair, because anyone can be a pilot.

scenes.caption: Always a boy.
scenes.say: Zara asks a story helper for a story about a pilot. Every story has a boy pilot.

scenes.caption: Pattern.
scenes.say: The text it learned from often had boy pilots. It copied the pattern.

scenes.caption: Fix.
scenes.say: Zara changes her prompt and tells her teacher. People can notice and fix bias.

question.prompt: A program can be unfair because of the data it learned from.
question.hint: Think about gaps and copied patterns.
question.explanation: Unbalanced or unfair data can make an AI unfair.

blocks.title: Zara's fair AI pledge
blocks.transcript: Zara's class has a voice reader. It listens and turns speech into text. They test it with ten voices from group A and ten from group B. It understands eight voices in group A. Only five in group B. Its training recordings had too few voices like group B. That is bias. They add more recordings from group B. Then they train and test again. Now it understands seven of ten in group B. The gap is smaller. A teacher keeps checking. People stay responsible, not the program. The class writes a pledge: be fair, check, ask and tell.
blocks.caption: Zara's class tests a voice reader for fairness and writes a pledge.

points: Bias is an unfair leaning in how an AI works
Unbalanced data or stereotypes can cause it
People can notice bias and fix it
blocks.say: Let us remember. Unbalanced data causes bias. AI can copy stereotypes. People can notice and fix it.

blocks.markdown: A **fair test** uses examples from many kinds of people.
blocks.say: To find bias, we test. A fair test uses examples from many kinds of people.

scenes.caption: Two groups.
scenes.say: Zara's class tests the voice reader with ten voices from group A and ten from group B.

scenes.caption: Results.
scenes.say: It understands eight of ten voices in group A. It understands only five of ten in group B.

scenes.caption: A gap.
scenes.say: The gap is big. The test shows the reader may be unfair, so it needs fixing.

blocks.title: Sort the test plans
blocks.goal: Move the 6 plans into Fair test or Not a fair test.

question.prompt: A reader works for 9 of 10 people in one group but only 4 of 10 in another. What does this suggest?
question.explanation: A big gap between groups suggests bias.

options.text: It may be unfair and needs fixing

blocks.markdown: Add missing examples. Train again. Test again.
blocks.say: To fix it, they add more recordings from group B. Then they train again and test again.
A high average can hide a problem. So we compare results for each group, not only the total.

scenes.caption: Add.
scenes.say: The class adds more recordings from group B and trains the reader again.

scenes.caption: Test.
scenes.say: They test again. Group B now scores seven out of ten. The gap is smaller.

scenes.caption: Keep checking.
scenes.say: They keep checking. Fairness is not finished after one fix.

blocks.title: Plan a fair test
instructions: Pick an AI helper you know, such as a voice helper.
List five different kinds of people or voices to test.
Write how you will compare the results for each group.
blocks.say: Now you try. Plan a fair test with a partner.

question.prompt: If an AI works well on average, it must work well for every group.
question.explanation: A high average can hide poor results for one group.

points: A fair test uses examples from many kinds of people
Compare the results for each group
Add missing examples, train and test again
blocks.say: Let us remember. Test on many kinds of people, compare groups, fix and test again.

terms.meaning: A test that uses examples from many kinds of people.
To look at things to see how they differ.
The middle or typical result.
A difference between two results.
A set of people with something in common.
To teach the program again.

mini_quiz.prompt: Why test on many kinds of people?
mini_quiz.explanation: A varied test shows who is left out.

options.text: To see if it is fair to everyone

mini_quiz.prompt: We should compare results for each group, not only the total.
What fixes a gap found by a test?

options.text: Adding missing examples and testing again

blocks.alt: A red spiral slide with green railings in a playground beside a lawn, with trees behind and a blue play surface
blocks.caption: A playground works well when people make safe rules for everyone. AI needs fair rules too.
blocks.credit: Photo by Singkai Lee on Unsplash
blocks.say: Playgrounds have rules so that everyone can play safely. AI needs rules too, made and followed by people.

blocks.markdown: **Responsible** people check AI and fix its mistakes.
blocks.say: An AI program cannot be responsible. The people who make it and use it are responsible.

scenes.caption: A zero.
scenes.say: An AI tool marks a quiz and gives Hamza zero. Hamza feels it is wrong.

scenes.caption: Check.
scenes.say: His teacher checks. The tool misread his handwriting. She fixes the mark.

scenes.caption: In charge.
scenes.say: People stay in charge. They check and take care of the results.

question.prompt: An AI tool harms someone by mistake. Who should make sure it is fixed?
question.hint: Think about who is in charge.
question.explanation: People make and use the tool, so they are responsible.

options.text: The people who make and use it

blocks.say: Personal data needs care. We ask permission before using someone's photo or voice to teach an AI.

blocks.markdown: Be open about using AI. Play the memory game.
blocks.say: People should also be told when AI is used, so they can ask questions. First, a memory game.

question.prompt: Tap the action that respects privacy.

items.label: Ask permission before using a photo

points: People are responsible for AI, not the AI itself
Be open about when AI is used
blocks.say: Let us remember. People are responsible. We ask permission, keep privacy and are open about AI.

terms.meaning: Having the duty to check and look after something.
Keeping personal information safe.
Being allowed to do something.
Being asked and saying yes.
Honest and clear about what is happening.
About a particular person.

mini_quiz.prompt: An AI program is responsible for its own mistakes.
What should we do before using someone's photo to teach an AI?
Why tell people when AI is being used?

options.text: So they can ask questions and check it

blocks.markdown: A **pledge** is a set of promises.
blocks.say: Zara's class writes a pledge about AI. A pledge is a set of promises that guide how we act.
Promise one: we will treat everyone fairly. Promise two: we will check what AI tells us.

blocks.markdown: Promise 3: ask and keep privacy. Promise 4: tell.
blocks.say: Promise three: we will ask permission and keep privacy. Promise four: we will tell a trusted adult about unfair results.

scenes.caption: Be fair.
scenes.say: Be fair. Everyone deserves AI that works well for them.

scenes.caption: Check and ask.
scenes.say: Check and ask. We check AI results, and we ask before using anyone's data.

scenes.caption: Tell.
scenes.say: Tell. If something seems unfair, we tell a trusted adult.

question.prompt: Put the steps of making a class AI pledge in order.

blocks.markdown: Used carefully, AI can help many people.
blocks.say: AI can do good when people use it carefully. It can read text aloud for people who find reading hard.

blocks.markdown: People and AI can work as a team.
blocks.say: It can help scientists sort photos of animals, and help doctors look at scans while a person checks.

scenes.caption: Reading help.
scenes.say: A reading helper reads a story aloud for a classmate who finds reading hard.

scenes.caption: Wildlife.
scenes.say: Scientists use image AI to sort wildlife photos, then check the unsure ones.

scenes.caption: Our goal.
scenes.say: Good AI is fair, tested and checked by people. That is our goal.

blocks.title: Our class pledge
instructions: Write three or four promises about fair and careful AI use.
Draw a symbol for each promise.
Say when you will review it, such as once each term.
blocks.say: Now you try. Write your own class pledge.

question.prompt: People should keep checking AI even when it usually works well.

points: Make a pledge: be fair, check, ask and tell
AI can do good when used carefully
People keep testing, checking and caring
blocks.say: Let us remember. Fair AI needs fair data, tests, responsible people and a clear pledge.
